options.B: The study of microorganisms inhabiting, creating, or contaminating food
options.C: The chemical composition of processed foods
options.D: The structural engineering of food storage facilities

explanation: Food microbiology specifically encompasses all microorganisms that inhabit, create, or contaminate food products, which is essential for public health nursing. [learn more](GST114_U3_T5#GST114_U3_T5_h1)

question: Why are lifestyle modifications such as regular exercise and balanced nutrition emphasized in holistic nursing care for oligomenorrhoea?

options.A: They completely replace the need for any diagnostic testing
options.B: They help ameliorate underlying metabolic disturbances like insulin resistance
options.C: They instantly cure pituitary adenomas
options.D: They prevent the normal production of estrogen

explanation: Lifestyle modifications improve insulin sensitivity and metabolic health, which are vital for managing endocrine disorders like PCOS. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T5#GNS216_U2_T5_h8)

question: What is the purpose of Intermittent Preventive Treatment in pregnancy (IPTp) using sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine in malaria-endemic regions?

options.A: To treat acute respiratory infections
options.B: To prevent malaria infection and its complications in the mother and placenta
options.C: To cure iron-deficiency anemia
options.D: To prevent gestational hypertension

explanation: IPTp with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine is administered to prevent malaria and protect the placenta from malaria-induced damage in endemic areas. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T006#GNS226_U1_T006_h6)

question: What is the main purpose of secondary wastewater treatment?

options.A: To add heavy metals back into the water
options.B: To use aerobic microorganisms to break down dissolved and suspended organic matter
options.C: To freeze the wastewater into solid blocks
options.D: To filter out visible plastic bottles

explanation: Secondary treatment utilizes aerobic microorganisms in aeration tanks or trickling filters to consume and break down organic pollutants. [learn more](GST114_U6_T4#GST114_U6_T4_h6)

question: At which type of facility would a nurse typically administer parenteral antibiotics and uterotonics for stabilization before transfer?

options.A: Basic Emergency Obstetric Care (BEmOC) facility
options.B: Tertiary blood bank laboratory only
options.C: Outpatient pediatric nutrition clinic
options.D: Immunization-only outreach post

explanation: BEmOC facilities are primary care settings equipped to perform signal functions including the administration of parenteral antibiotics and uterotonics. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T009#GNS226_U1_T009_h2)

question: Why are accurate recording and reporting vital for the primary health care system?

options.A: They guarantee that health workers receive higher salaries.
options.B: They eliminate the need for physical patient examinations.
options.C: They ensure continuity of care and support public health surveillance and planning.
options.D: They replace the need for verbal communication among healthcare teams.

explanation: Reliable documentation ensures continuous care for patients and supplies essential data for public health tracking and resource allocation. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T2#GNS124_U6_T2_h1)

question: What was a major limitation of health systems inherited by many developing nations, such as Nigeria, prior to the Alma-Ata Declaration?

options.A: Excessive focus on rural health posts
options.B: Overemphasis on urban-based, curative medicine
options.C: Complete absence of any medical personnel
options.D: Too much emphasis on community participation

explanation: Pre-existing colonial and early post-colonial health systems heavily favored expensive, urban-based curative care while neglecting vulnerable rural populations. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T5#GNS124_U1_T5_h1)
